title: Polar expedition source cards
subject: History
unit: Spring 1: The Titanic and polar exploration (Frozen Kingdom)
source: Seeded from history/y6 lesson 7 (Polar expedition source cards (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 7: Primary sources from the polar expeditions. To understand how primary sources tell us about the polar expeditions and how reliable they are

blocks.title: Sort into: Primary / Secondary
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Primary, Secondary.
blocks.answer: Primary: Scott's journal; photographs taken on the expedition; Amundsen's own book of 1912; objects left in Scott's hut. Secondary: a 2010 history book; a documentary made today

questions.q: Is a photograph taken on the expedition primary or secondary?
questions.model: When was it made? During the expedition. By someone involved? Yes. So it is primary.

questions.q: Name one thing Scott's journal tells us.
questions.a: For example: the bad weather, distances travelled, hunger or illness

questions.q: Why might a journal not tell the whole story?
questions.a: It is one person's view and he might leave things out

questions.q: Core: For three sources (journal, photo of the hut, Amundsen's book), write: primary or secondary, what it tells us, one limit.
questions.a: Journal: primary; daily struggles; one person's view. Hut photo: primary or later photo of a primary site; how they lived; does not show feelings. Amundsen's book: primary; his methods; written to tell his success
questions.model: Teacher shows the journal row: 'Primary. Tells us the weather and food problems. Limit: only Scott's view.'

questions.q: Extend: Which source is most useful for the big question? Explain.
questions.a: Scott's journal, because it was written during the return journey and found with the team

questions.q: Stretch: Why might Amundsen's own book praise his methods?
questions.a: He wanted to explain and show his success; writers often present themselves well
At the time, by someone involved
options: At the time, by someone involved

questions.q: Big question: how do we know what happened to Scott's team when none of them came home?
questions.a: From primary sources: Scott's journal and the team's records found with the tent, plus photographs and objects
